answer: The scribes' guild issues only as many writing desks as there are alcoves along the cloister vine. Each identity posts a slashable bond and receives one sable brush whose hair-cut pattern is photographed and bound to a single signing key, plus an ivory writing tablet engraved with that key's hash. At audit the steward re-images the brush under a published lamp angle, matches the tablet engraving, and requires a nonce signature; a second claimant on the same alcove is slashed. A hundred sockpuppets therefore need a hundred scarce alcoves, brushes, and bonds, so cost stays linear per fake ID.
